title: Three Steps at a Time: Learning Representations from Action Sequences in Contrastive RL
abstract: arXiv:2608.30640v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While self-supervised approaches to reinforcement learning have achieved strong results by learning representations of states and actions, a key open question is the time scale over which actions should be modeled. Departing from the standard formulation relying on single-step actions, we extend contrastive reinforcement learning (CRL), a prototypical self-supervised method, to operate over action chunks, and find that this results in large, pervasive gains across established offline and online benchmarks: +31.7% and +93.1% across 18 and 11 environments respectively. While action-chunking-driven gains are generally explained through the ability to model non-Markovian, temporally extended policies, and to propagate unbiased multi-step returns, interestingly, we find that these arguments only partially apply to CRL. Our empirical studies suggest that, in the context of CRL, an action chunk carries more information about the goal than a sin

translated_title: 每次三步：在对比强化学习中从动作序列学习表征
translated_abstract: 尽管强化学习的自监督方法通过学习状态和动作的表征已经取得了优异的成绩，但一个关键的开放性问题是应该在什么时间尺度上对动作进行建模。我们突破了依赖单步动作的标准形式，将对比强化学习（CRL）这一典型的自监督方法扩展到动作块上，发现在既有的离线和在线基准测试中均能带来巨大而普遍的性能提升：分别在18个和11个环境中获得+31.7%和+93.1%的提升。虽然动作分块带来的收益通常被解释为能够建模非马尔可夫的、时间上延展的策略，以及能够传播无偏的多步回报，但有趣的是，我们发现这些论点仅部分适用于CRL。我们的实证研究表明，在CRL的背景下，一个动作块比单个动作携带更多关于目标的信息……
tldr: 本文的核心创新是将对比强化学习（CRL）从单步动作扩展到动作块上进行表征学习，在离线和在线基准上分别取得+31.7%和+93.1%的大幅提升，并发现动作块比单步动作携带更多目标信息是其成功的关键。
en_tdlr: Extending contrastive RL to learn representations from action chunks instead of single-step actions yields large gains (+31.7% offline, +93.1% online) across benchmarks, with action chunks carrying more goal information than single actions.
